correctness.rationale: Increasing paths of length three give exactly (abc,bcd,abg+adf+ecd) in positions (14,25,15); the higher three input entries contribute q³ freely. For (A,B)≠(0,0) one chooses b,c nonzero and solves uniquely for a,d; the last output is a nonzero linear functional with q² lifts. At A=B=0, there are H=q⁴−(q−1)²(q²−1) eligible quadruples. A nonzero last functional occurs in three disjoint cases: ad≠0 and bc=0, or ad=0 with ab≠0 (forcing d=c=0), or ad=0 with cd≠0 (forcing a=b=0). They give L=(q−1)²(2q+1) quadruples. A nonzero C has q⁵L lifts; at zero the count is q⁵[L+q(H−L)], as claimed. The counts are positive and strictly increasing in the stated order for q≥2, and with target multiplicities q(q²−1), q−1, 1 their sum is q¹⁰. In characteristic three the binomial identity holds since I commutes with X. The filtration 1+N₅^i bounds the lower central series in one direction by commutator degree, and elementary matrix commutators generate each permitted superdiagonal in the other; thus γ₃=1+N₅³.
